messages:
alex: noticed a spike of apiserver 503s in eu-west2 while a GPU onboarding wave was running. controller-manager pod restarts + leader change around the same time. anyone else seeing this?
priya: yup saw alerts at 10:04 UTC. metrics show apiserver request latency jumped then connections dropped.
lucas: stack: etcd leader churn -> apiserver timeout -> controller-manager reconcile backlog. GPU attach churn seems to correlate with NAT SNAT exhaustion in that region.
alex: logs excerpt:```kube-apiserver: E1004 10:04:22.123 request.go:123] apiserver request timeout: 30s``````controller-manager: panic: failed to update lease: connection refused``````etcd: renewed leader from host-a to host-b at 10:04:15``````
sre-bot: deploy triggered: gpu-provisioner/v2 roll 2026-10-04T10:03:00Z by deploy-bot
jen: oof. the provisioner rollout might have bumped node attach traffic + NAT ports. our NAT pools in eu-west2 were already near 85% due to model egress bursts.
priya: quick mitigation idea: throttle GPU attach concurrency for that region and enable apiserver client-side circuit-breaker. we can also move lower-priority onboarding to a different region temp.
lucas: agree. also recommend reducing apiserver watch-fanout by enabling watch aggregation for provisioner controller during scale bursts.
alex: can someone patch the provisioner config to max 8 simultaneous attaches (was 32)? that should spread load.
jen: i'll open a quick PR to change concurrency and add an opt-in per-region cap. linking patch: https://git.internal/r/redwood/gpu-provisioner/pulls/412
priya: pasted commands I ran to confirm SNAT saturation:```kubectl --context=eu-west2 get svc -n kube-system | grep nat && sudo iptables -t nat -L -n | grep ESTABLISHED``` nothing fancy but shows ephemeral port utilization at 91% on gateway-2.
lucas: fallback plan for product: route non-critical user requests to dedicated-cpu nodes if apiserver latency > 500ms for 2m. We have routing flags in runtime to prefer cheap-cpu for batch jobs.
alex: cost note: if we move bursts to other regions or spin up larger NATs, we'll incur cross-region bandwidth + NAT GW costs. estimates?
jen: rough: adding a /24 NAT pool equivalent + buffer ~ $1.8k/month for eu-west2. moving onboarding to another region adds egress (~$0.12/GB) but is temporary.
priya: postmortem checklist volunteers? need: root cause correlation (attach churn -> nat -> etcd leader), remediation (throttle + watch agg), longer-term (pre-warm node pool, better nat autoscale, metrics for attach concurrency), rollout safety (feature flags).
lucas: i'll own pre-warm proposal and metrics. jen can handle provisioner config. alex will draft the customer-facing note if any SLA blips.
sre-bot: incident created: INC-2026-847 linked to thread 3777401234
deploy-bot: rolled back gpu-provisioner/v2 canary on eu-west2 at 10:08 UTC :thumbsup:
alex: rollback reduced attach rate immediately; apiserver latency trending down. monitoring -> keep an eye for leader flips.
priya: agreed. schedule a wg meeting tomorrow 09:00 UTC to discuss NAT autoscale thresholds and controller backpressure.
jen: adding action items to the incident doc.
lucas: note to self: add a prometheus alert for attach_concurrency > 20 sustained for 1m in region labels.
alex: thanks all. final action: short-term throttle + rollback applied, medium-term pre-warm + nat autoscale, long-term redesign provisioner to backoff more aggressively and prefer in-region pre-warmed instances. :white_check_mark:
jen: :+1:
priya: :thumbsup:
